To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a combination of 5-aminolevulinic acid and photofrin for fluorescence-guided resection of high-grade gliomas is safe and feasible and that the use of 5-amlminolevulinic for fluorescence-guided biopsy is safe and may be feasible.
the presence of IgA deposits in the mesangium of the renal glomeruli is a marker of IgAN, and the presence of IgAN is associated with a high risk of renal disease progression.

the use of a novel, noninvasive method of measuring renal blood flow, renal arterial Doppler ultrasonography, in patients with type 2 diabetes and proteinuria is feasible, reproducible, and correlates with the degree of albuminuria.

the study of the role of the immune system in the pathogenesis of IgAN.
the study of the relationship between the immune system and the development of atherosclerosis.
the role of mesangial IgA deposition in the progression of IgAN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a lack of sufficient evidence for the use of IgA nephropathy-specific drugs in the management of IgA nephritis.
the evidence does not support the use of a specific treatment for IgA nephropathy, but the evidence does not rule out that a particular treatment is beneficial either.
there is insufficient evidence to suggest a link between IgA nephropathy and the development of cancer in patients with this condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the expression of the genes encoding the three subunits of the TCR is regulated by a common mechanism.
we have demonstrated that a combination of a novel, highly sensitive and specific, and non-invasive imaging modality (PET/CT) can detect early changes in the kidney in patients with diabetes.
we have demonstrated that the presence of IgA in the glomerulus is a marker for disease activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no clear guidelines for the use of anticoagulation in patients with CKD.
the presence of mesangial IgA deposition does not predict progression of IgA nephropathy, and that the presence of IgA deposition in mesangial areas does not predict the presence of IgM deposition.
the immune system plays an important role in the progression of kidney disease.
